The actual test logic works correctly on the real, force-bucketed Convert experience for both arms. Every failure surfaced in the raw Playwright runs traces back to one of: (1) a wrong URL supplied in the ticket, (2) known local-injection artifacts from a co-running live test (cre-t-116), (3) one isolated WebKit page-load flake, or (4) a stale/unrelated local CSS file that does not affect the live site. No functional defect was found in the actual price-discount logic itself.

Part 1 (live preview URLs) ran on all 6; Part 2 (local code injection) ran on the 4 desktop browsers, matching this client's established convention.

What this test does

Reduces published listing prices sitewide (default view, Dogs/Cats tabs, ZIP filter, and combinations, including listings 8-10 inside "Show More") by a fixed percentage: V1 13.5% off, V2 32.9% off. No discount is shown once a user selects a specific breed; reverting to "All Breeds" re-applies it. The code patches window.fetch to read live per-provider prices, inserts a .cre-t-143-discounted-price span next to each real price, and hides the original via CSS.

BUG-05 (NEW) — local v2.css file is stale/unrelated content (repo mismatch, not a live bug)

v2.css (the file currently mapped to the V2 arm per this session's instruction) is leftover content from an unrelated pay.com.au test (cre-t-13 modal styling) — it contains no rule to hide the original price. vB.css (V1) has the correct rule. The va3.css/va3.js files still on disk are ALSO not a valid substitute — va3.css is actually cre-t-164 (Rearrange Listings) CSS, a different test entirely.

Locally injecting the real, current v2.js + v2.css pairing did not show a visible duplicate-price defect in testing — but that result is confounded by cre-t-116's live CSS coincidentally hiding the untagged original price anyway during local injection (see the "local-injection artifacts" note below), so it is not reliable evidence that v2.css is fine.

Cross-referencing the real V2 force-preview URL (Part 1, screenshot above): the discount renders correctly there with the original properly hidden — meaning Convert is serving a different, correct CSS live for V2 than what's in this repo's v2.css.

Not a live bug — production is fine. But v2.css in the repo should be corrected to match the real deployed CSS so a future redeploy from this repo doesn't accidentally ship the wrong file.

BUG-02 — shared global JS guard names between vB.js and v2.js (RECONFIRMED, unchanged, zero live impact)

vB.js and v2.js still guard their one-time init behind the same global flags (window.cre_t_143_fetchPatched, window.cre_t_143_priceObserverStarted). Reconfirmed live 2026-09-11, all 4 desktop browsers, same as the 2026-09-10 finding. In production only one arm is ever served per visitor, so there is no user-facing impact — flagged only as a low-priority cleanup item.

BUG-03 — still an OPEN QUESTION, still unanswered

Does V2 need to target "Small, mixed breed" specifically, or does the default/unfiltered view already represent it? testdetail.md's new Q&A section answers several other open questions (breed-revert reapplication: yes; Google Audiences: not needed) but does not address this one. The code has no per-breed-value matching logic — it is a blanket on/off switch keyed on "any breed selected at all," unchanged from the first pass. Same question still applies to V1's "Mid-size, mixed breed" text. Needs a direct answer before this can be closed out either way.

What was verified as correct

  • Both arms correctly discount every priced listing card, including the 3 tail cards revealed by "Show More" — math is exact to the discount percentage against the site's own live quote price.
  • Discount correctly persists across Dogs/Cats tab switches and ZIP-filter entry, in both the real live preview experience and local code injection.
  • Selecting a breed suppresses the discount entirely, and reverting to "All Breeds" correctly re-applies it — the newly-confirmed ticket requirement — verified via the URL-param method in both arms, all 4 desktop browsers.
  • No console/page errors, no duplicate-id regressions, idempotent on re-injection.
  • V2's real force-preview URL (167) is correct and fully working end to end.

Methodology notes

  • Per instruction, preview links were checked first (Part 1), then local code (Part 2).
  • All browser checks used fresh Playwright browser.newContext() instances (no shared cookies/state between checks) — equivalent to a private/incognito window each time.
  • TC-04's local-injection failures reproduce a known artifact already documented from the 2026-09-10 pass: cre-t-116 is live at 100% traffic for organic visitors and its CSS hides any freshly-injected span in the price slot; this does not occur once a session is genuinely bucketed into CRE-T-143 (confirmed again via the real force-preview URLs in Part 1).
  • The MUI breed-picker widget could not be driven end-to-end automatically this pass — see the test-harness note in _client-notes.md for the specific gap (ZIP input's synthetic change event doesn't reliably trigger the site's async ZIP validation).
